key_insight: OmniCapBench proposes a more rigorous way to evaluate fine-grained audio-visual captioning by combining broad coverage with localized diagnostics. It aims to reveal where multimodal large language models succeed or fail, instead of relying on unstable or overly coarse benchmark scores.
problem_solved: Existing audio-visual captioning benchmarks force a trade-off: full-caption evaluation captures overall quality but misses precise error localization, while local probes are detailed but too narrow. This paper addresses the lack of a stable, deep-structured evaluation framework for measuring fine-grained audio-visual reasoning.
method: Introduces OmniCapBench, a deep-structured benchmark for evaluating audio-visual captioning at multiple levels of granularity.
Balances global caption assessment with localized diagnostic probes to better identify capability limits.
Avoids relying on unconstrained LLM judges by aiming for more structured and stable evaluation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a clearer way to diagnose multimodal model weaknesses and compare systems more reliably. It can guide model development, error analysis, and more trustworthy evaluation of continuous audio-visual reasoning.
